payload.title: [calls-authz-1] createCall performs no conversation-membership check — any user can ring anyone and bind a call ...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING calls-authz-1 (high/authz, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/calls/call-control-plane.ts
LINES: 243-303

WHAT: createCall accepts an arbitrary `conversationId` and arbitrary `inviteeUserIds` with no check that the creator is a member of that conversation, that invitees are conversation members, or any policy-hook gate. The gateway's #handleCallCommand (gateway.ts 1676-1714) only requires an authenticated, active principal (#activePrincipalForFrame) before forwarding to plane.createCall — there is no assertCan*/membership call for any call op, unlike signal/object paths. The control plane stores conversationId on the room/events (lines 265, 277) but never validates it.

IMPACT: Any authenticated tenant user can: (1) create a call against any conversationId they are not part of, and (2) send ringing CallInvites to any userId in the tenant — unsolicited-call/ring spam and harassment, plus a path to attach call activity/events to conversations the actor cannot otherwise access. The invitee then has a legitimate path to join (calls-authz is invite-based), so this also widens who can pull others into a media session.

SUGGESTED FIX: In #handleCallCommand's create branch (or inside createCall via an injected membership reader), assert the creator is a member of conversationId and that each invitee is a co-member, using the same tenantMembershipReader/policy-hook machinery the signal/object paths use. Reject with auth.forbidden otherwise.
